Time Inc. and Warner Communications (WCI) entered into an $18 billion merger agreement on March 4, 1989, to create the world's largest media conglomerate. The initial agreement was presented as a stock-for-stock "merger of equals" that would result in the establishment of a new company, with the CEOs of both companies, Richard Munro and Steve Ross, sharing the position of Co-CEO. Reactions to the merger with mixed and concerns emerged from the combination of the businesses' cable units. deal faced setbacks from Paramount Communications, which contested the transaction.
Following these challenges, Time Inc. changed its deal with Warner, turning the planned merger into a leveraged acquisition in which Time would take a 51% controlling interest in Warner Communications and purchase the remaining shares months later. In June 1989, Paramount Communications launched a hostile takeover bid for Time, offering $12.2 billion, or $200 per share. Time Inc. turned down the offer, prompting Paramount to file two lawsuits in Delaware. The case, Paramount Communications v. Time Inc., went on for several weeks before ending in Time’s favor. In August 1989, Time had secured its controlling interest in Warner Communications. Since Time was the buyer, its financial results were included in the 1989 fiscal year for Time Warner. The remaining shares of Warner were acquired on January 10, 1990, though Time Warner had already been operating since August 1989.
By 1992, Time Warner consolidated its competing publishing units and cable businesses into the Time Warner Book Group and Time Warner Cable. Turner Broadcasting System was acquired on October 10, 1996, and Time Warner gained an assortment of cable channels. A consequential event in the company's history was its unsuccessful merger with America Online (AOL). Despite promises for synergies, heavy losses occurred leading to a significant drawdown in assets. Time was spun off in 2014, while the Time Warner named was retired on June 15, 2018, after AT&T closed its purchase of the business.
